The fix is to convert epoch-millisecond timestamps and keep one row per txn_id, which keeps silver and the gold tables free of double-counted spend.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.72, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS WITH src AS (SELECT txn_id, customer_id, merchant_id, amount, ingest_ts, CASE WHEN regexp_full_match(txn_ts, '^[0-9]+$') THEN epoch_ms(CAST(txn_ts AS BIGINT)) ELSE CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) END AS ts FROM raw_transactions WHERE status = 'POSTED'), dedup AS (SELECT * FROM src QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY txn_id ORDER BY ingest_ts, ts) = 1) SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, ts AS txn_ts, CAST(ts AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM dedup;"}}
